title: Build Charts and Format a Budget Spreadsheet
description: Create a monthly budget spreadsheet with charts, sorting, filtering, and professional formatting in Excel.
objective: Students will build a formatted monthly budget spreadsheet, create Column, Pie, and Line charts from data, apply sorting and filtering, and set up the worksheet for printing with headers and footers.

steps.title: Create the Budget Data Table
steps.instructions:
Open Microsoft Excel and create a new blank workbook.

1. **Rename** the first worksheet to "Budget" (double-click the Sheet1 tab at the bottom and type "Budget").
2. In cell **A1**, type: **Monthly Budget — Ananya's Household — Bhopal**
3. Select A1:D1, click **Merge & Center**, make it **Bold**, font size **14**.

4. Starting from **Row 3**, enter the following data:

| | A (Category) | B (Budgeted Rs.) | C (Actual Rs.) | D (Difference Rs.) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | **Category** | **Budgeted** | **Actual** | **Difference** |
| 4 | Rent | 8000 | 8000 | |
| 5 | Groceries | 5000 | 5800 | |
| 6 | Transport | 2500 | 2200 | |
| 7 | Electricity | 1500 | 1800 | |
| 8 | Phone/Internet | 1000 | 1000 | |
| 9 | Clothing | 2000 | 1500 | |
| 10 | Entertainment | 1500 | 2200 | |
| 11 | Education | 3000 | 3000 | |
| 12 | Medical | 1000 | 500 | |
| 13 | Savings | 4500 | 3500 | |
| 14 | **Total** | | | |

5. Format the header row (Row 3): **Bold**, **Center-aligned**, dark blue background with white text.
6. Apply **Currency format** to columns B and C (right-click > Format Cells > Number > Currency, symbol: Rs.).
7. In cell **D4**, type: `=B4-C4` and drag down to D13.
8. In cells B14, C14, D14, use `=SUM()` to total each column.
9. Apply **All Borders** to the entire table (A3:D14).

steps.title: Create a Column Chart
steps.instructions:
Create a chart comparing budgeted vs actual expenses.

1. Select the data range **A3:C13** (categories, budgeted, and actual amounts — do NOT include the Total row).
2. Go to **Insert** tab > **Charts** group > click **Column Chart** > select **Clustered Column**.
3. A chart appears on your worksheet.

**Add chart elements:**
4. Click on the chart. Click the **Chart Elements** button (+ icon next to the chart).
5. Check **Chart Title** and type: **Budgeted vs Actual Expenses**
6. Check **Axis Titles**:
   - Horizontal axis title: **Expense Category**
   - Vertical axis title: **Amount (Rs.)**
7. Check **Legend** (it should show two bars: Budgeted and Actual).
8. Check **Data Labels** to show values on top of each bar.

**Position the chart:**
9. Click and drag the chart to position it below the data table (around row 16).
10. Resize it by dragging a corner handle to make it wider and easier to read.

The chart should clearly show which categories went over budget (Actual bar taller than Budgeted bar) and which stayed under budget.

steps.title: Create a Pie Chart
steps.instructions:
Create a pie chart showing how the actual spending is distributed across categories.

1. Select **A3:A13** (category names). Hold **Ctrl** and also select **C3:C13** (actual amounts). This selects two non-adjacent ranges.
2. Go to **Insert** > **Pie Chart** > select **2-D Pie**.
3. A pie chart appears.

**Customize the pie chart:**
4. Click the chart, then click the **Chart Elements** button (+).
5. Add **Chart Title**: **Actual Spending Distribution**
6. Add **Data Labels** > select **Percentage** (this shows what percentage of total each category represents).
7. Remove the Legend if the data labels are clear enough, or keep it for reference.

**Format the chart:**
8. Click on any slice of the pie chart. Right-click > **Format Data Series**.
9. Try pulling out one slice (e.g., Rent) by clicking on it once, then dragging it slightly outward to create an "exploded" effect.
10. Position this chart next to or below the Column chart.

Note: The Pie chart should only have one data series (Actual amounts). This is why Pie charts are best for showing parts of a whole.

steps.title: Apply Sorting and Filtering
steps.instructions:
Practice sorting and filtering the budget data.

**Sorting:**
1. Click anywhere in the data table (A3:D13).
2. Go to **Data** tab > click **Sort**.
3. Sort by **Actual** (Column C) in **Largest to Smallest** order.
4. Click **OK**. Notice how the rows rearrange — Rent should be at the top.
5. Observe that the charts automatically update to reflect the new order.

**Filtering:**
6. Click anywhere in the data table.
7. Go to **Data** tab > click **Filter**.
8. Small dropdown arrows appear in the header row.
9. Click the dropdown arrow on column C (**Actual**).
10. Select **Number Filters** > **Greater Than** > type **2000** > click OK.
11. Only categories with actual spending above Rs. 2000 are now visible.
12. Notice the row numbers are blue — this means some rows are hidden (filtered out).
13. To clear the filter: click the dropdown arrow on column C again > click **Clear Filter From "Actual"**.
14. To remove all filters: go to **Data** > click **Filter** again to toggle it off.

**Important:** Filtering **hides** rows; it does **not delete** them. All your data is safe.

steps.title: Set Up Printing and Save
steps.instructions:
Prepare the worksheet for professional printing.

**Page Setup:**
1. Go to **Page Layout** tab.
2. Set **Orientation** to **Landscape** (since we have charts that are wide).
3. Set **Margins** to **Narrow** for more space.

**Print Area:**
4. Select all the data and charts you want to print.
5. Go to Page Layout > **Print Area** > **Set Print Area**.

**Headers and Footers:**
6. Go to **Insert** > **Header & Footer**.
7. In the **center header section**, type: **Monthly Budget Report — TechPath Institute**
8. Click on the **footer** area. In the center section, type: `Page &[Page] of &[Pages]`
9. In the right footer section, click the **Date** button to insert `&[Date]`.
10. Click anywhere in the worksheet to exit header/footer editing.

**Freeze Panes:**
11. Click on cell **A4** (first data row).
12. Go to **View** > **Freeze Panes** > **Freeze Panes**.
13. Now when you scroll down, rows 1-3 (title and headers) stay visible.

**Print Preview and Save:**
14. Press **Ctrl + P** to open Print Preview.
15. Verify that the data table and charts appear correctly.
16. Check that the header and footer are visible.
17. Close Print Preview.
18. Save the workbook as `Budget_Charts.xlsx` (press Ctrl + S).

Congratulations! You have created a complete budget spreadsheet with formulas, charts, sorting, filtering, and print setup.
